At least three people were killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike targeting Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province, Tolo News reported on Monday, citing a provincial official.The military strike is supposedly in retaliation for suicide bombing at a police station compound in northwestern Pakistan, raising fears that tensions between the neighbouring nations could once again turn into open fighting.Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action.Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, ahead of the imminent Pakistani strikes, had warned Islamabad against carrying out strikes inside Afghanistan, saying Kabul would respond militarily if its territory is attacked.In an interview with Al Arabiya English, Mujahid rejected Pakistan's allegations that militant groups based in Afghanistan recruit, train and launch attacks against Pakistan.“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” Mujahid said.He said any Pakistani military operation inside Afghanistan would amount to a violation of Afghan sovereignty and could trigger a strong response from Kabul.Mujahid was responding to comments by a Pakistani military spokesperson, who had told Al Arabiya English that militant groups were using Afghan territory to recruit, train and arm fighters before sending them into Pakistan.Mujahid rejected those allegations and said the Taliban administration does not allow the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , or TTP, to operate from Afghan soil.He also denied that the Taliban government supports armed groups carrying out attacks against other countries. Instead, Mujahid said Pakistan should examine its own internal security problems, arguing that violence involving the TTP and Baloch armed groups existed before the Taliban returned to power in 2021.Pakistan has repeatedly accused militant groups of operating from Afghanistan and has pressed Kabul to take action against them. The Taliban has consistently denied allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.Despite his warning of military retaliation, Mujahid said Kabul was still willing to engage with Islamabad through dialogue.He called for stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements and greater bilateral cooperation to address security concerns along the two countries' border.Mujahid also backed a possible mediation role for Saudi Arabia, saying Riyadh has good relations with both Afghanistan and Pakistan and could help the two sides resolve their differences.Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border. The latest airstrike, coming amid fresh security concerns, risks further worsening those ties and could lead to another confrontation between the neighbours.
Article Summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action. Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border.

Article Title: Jailed former Pak PM Imran Khan undergoes medical check-up amid concerns over health
Article Text:
Imran Khan

Geo News

Jailed former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan underwent a medical check-up at Adiala Jail amid concerns over his health, according to a media report on Sunday.Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 following his conviction in a corruption case and is currently lodged at the high-security Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi.According to, a specialist team from the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) examined Khan at the jail. The check-up included assessments of his blood pressure, cholesterol levels and eyesight.The medical team was led by a PIMS doctor, with medical staff from the Adiala Jail hospital assisting during the examination, the report said.Khan has previously complained of an eye condition and has been taken to PIMS several times for treatment. His supporters have alleged that his health has deteriorated due to inadequate medical care, a claim that prison authorities have repeatedly rejected.The Supreme Court had ordered on August 18 that Khan be shifted to a private medical facility for treatment. However, he was taken to PIMS, where he underwent medical tests before being returned to jail, news agency ANI cited.His Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party has sought his transfer to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital for a detailed medical examination and treatment, while raising concerns over his health.The party has also announced a September 27 demonstration seeking Khan's release.Khan has faced multiple legal cases since his removal as prime minister through a no-confidence vote in April 2022, with his health and conditions of detention remaining a recurring issue in Pakistan's political discourse.
Article Summary: Imran Khan, 73, has been in jail since 2023 following his conviction in a corruption case. Khan has previously complained of an eye condition and has been taken to PIMS several times for treatment. His supporters have alleged that his health has deteriorated due to inadequate medical care.

Article Title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan's sister Aleema arrested in Lahore ahead of Sept 27 PTI march
Article Text:
Aleema Khan arrested ahead of planned Imran Khan-founded PTI march

Long-imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan 's sister, Aleema Khan, was arrested from her home in Lahore on Sunday ahead of a planned march on September 27.Police arrested Aleema as she was planning a protest march organised by Imran Khan-founded Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI). A PTI spokesperson confirmed her arrest to Reuters.A notification issued by Lahore's district administration said Aleema Khan had been arrested and sent to jail for 30 days, citing concerns over public safety.“According to intelligence reports, her presence at any public place will pose a grave threat to public safety,” the notification said.Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has planned a march to Islamabad next week, demanding the former prime minister's release.Pakistan interior minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Saturday that the government would take all possible measures to prevent the protest march.Zulfi Bukhari, a close aide to Imran Khan, condemned Aleema's arrest as “absolutely despicable”.“The fear of the 27th protest is clearly taking its toll,” Bukhari said.The World Cup-winning cricket captain and former prime minister Imran Khan has been imprisoned for more than three years.Khan's family, including his two sons, have repeatedly expressed concern over his health and alleged a conspiracy involving Pakistan's de facto leader and military chief Asim Munir.
Article Summary: Aleema Khan arrested ahead of planned Imran Khan-founded PTI march. Imran Khan's sister sent to jail for 30 days, citing concerns over public safety. Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) has planned a march to Islamabad next week.

Article Title: Pakistan foreign minister dials Iranian counterpart, urges uninterrupted energy supplies and safe passage of ships
Article Text:
Abbas Araghchi and Ishaq Dar (File photo)

(With PTI inputs)

Pakistan’s foreign minister Ishaq Dar on Saturday urged his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, that Tehran must ensure “uninterrupted energy supplies” and the “safe and expeditious passage of ships”, amid concerns over disruptions to crucial waterways in the Middle East.Dar, who also serves as Pakistan’s deputy prime minister, held a telephonic conversation with Araghchi to discuss the latest regional developments, according to a statement from Pakistan’s Foreign Office (FO) on X.During the call, Dar “stressed the importance of uninterrupted energy supplies and the safe and expeditious passage of ships, particularly given their implications for developing countries and global supply chains”.He also underscored that “dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means to ensure peace and stability in the region”, the FO noted.The two ministers agreed to maintain close cooperation and meet in New York City next week on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, the foreign office added.The conversation came amid growing concerns over the safety of oil supply routes as tensions escalate around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb, as well as uncertainty surrounding the United States-Iran war, which began on February 28.The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, while Bab al-Mandeb connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden.The Strait of Hormuz has been under a virtual Iranian blockade since March, with Tehran effectively restricting passage through the critical maritime corridor in retaliation for US-Israeli attacks on Iran that triggered the conflict.Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi forces, aligned with Tehran, have imposed a de facto blockade on the Bab al-Mandeb Strait since July, seizing key shoreline territory and Mayun Island while specifically targeting Saudi-linked shipping and energy infrastructure.
Article Summary: Pakistan’s foreign minister Ishaq Dar urged his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, that Tehran must ensure ‘uninterrupted energy supplies’ Dar also underscored that “dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means to ensure peace and stability in the region’

Article Title: 'We want to go home': Hindu minor sisters abducted, converted, married in Pakistan's Sindh
Article Text:
Pakistan: Two minor Hindu sisters allegedly abducted, converted and forced into marriage

Sindh at centre of concern over minority girls

The alleged abduction and forced conversion of two minor Hindu sisters in Pakistan's Sindh province has triggered fresh concern among minority rights group, with one organisation calling for an independent probe and safeguards for the girls.According to Voice of Pakistan Minority, Roopi, 13 and Seeta, 14, were allegedly taken from Ibrahim Colony in Tando Allahyar district and later converted to Islam and married to two Muslim men, Amjad Solangi and Mansood Solangi.The sisters were subsequently brought before a court in Tando Allahyar in an abduction case. Instead of sending them back to their family, the court placed them in a safe house, VOPM said.The rights group said the girls appeared distressed outside the court and were heard pleading to be taken home. A video circulating online also purportedly showed the sisters saying, “Let us go to our parents” and “We want to go home.”VOPM said the circumstances surrounding the case made it important that the sisters be heard independently, without anyone who could influence or intimidate them.“The state must interview Roopi and Seeta in a child-sensitive environment, away from alleged husbands, religious figures, intermediaries or anyone who could pressure them.Officials must allow the girls to speak freely and must provide them independent legal support and protection,” VOPM said.The organisation called for an urgent, independent and transparent investigation into the allegations.The case has also renewed attention on the vulnerability of Hindu families in Sindh, which has Pakistan's largest Hindu population. VOPM said the problem is particularly acute in rural areas, where poverty, caste discrimination and limited access to legal assistance can leave minority families vulnerable.“This case has caused deep anxiety among Hindu communities in Sindh. Sindh hosts Pakistan’s largest Hindu population, particularly in rural districts where many Hindu families face poverty, caste discrimination and weak access to legal help,” it said.Rights groups have for years raised concerns over allegations involving the abduction, conversion and marriage of minority girls in Pakistan.VOPM cited data from the Centre for Social Justice, included in UK government material, which recorded 421 such cases involving minority girls and women between 2021 and 2024. Hindu women and girls accounted for 282 of those cases, while 72 per cent were reported from Sindh.The organisation said Pakistani authorities recorded at least 83 cases in 2024 alone, with Hindu girls making up 63 per cent of the victims.The concern extends beyond the figures. VOPM also referred to warnings by UN experts in 2026 that nearly 80 per cent of reported cases involving alleged forced conversion through marriage in Pakistan during 2025 took place in Sindh. About 75 per cent of the victims were reportedly Hindus.For VOPM, the immediate focus remains on the two sisters and whether they can speak freely about what happened to them.“Roopi and Seeta’s reported call to return home demands attention. Their protection, age, dignity, and freedom must come before every other consideration,” the VOPM noted.
Article Summary: Roopi, 13 and Seeta, 14, allegedly taken from Ibrahim Colony in Tando Allahyar district. They were allegedly converted to Islam and married to two Muslim men. Rights group calls for an independent probe and safeguards for the girls.

Article Title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa bombing: Pakistan identifies 'Afghan national' among attackers
Article Text:
The blast was reported near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

(With PTI inputs)

Pakistani officials said Saturday that one of the suicide bombers who targeted a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mosque was an Afghan national.The explosions killed at least 21 people—including 15 police officers offering Friday prayers at the mosque—and injured 103 others, with police personnel making up the majority of the casualties.According to an investigator, in addition to the attacker identified as an Afghan citizen, efforts to identify a second bomber are ongoing. A joint probe team consisting of local police, the counter-terrorism department, the Elite Force, and security forces is currently investigating the attack.During Friday's assault, the bombers drove an explosives-laden vehicle into the mosque before storming nearby police facilities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Kohat district.Pakistani security authorities have repeatedly accused "Afghanistan-based militant groups" of threatening regional security through terrorism and cross-border infiltration. Islamabad has further accused the Afghan Taliban of harbouring elements linked to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP)—allegations the Afghan Taliban denies.The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa attack was claimed by Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a little-known alliance formed last April that includes the Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group, Harakat Inqilab-e-Islami Pakistan, and Lashkar-e-Islam.
Article Summary: One of the suicide bombers who targeted a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mosque was an Afghan national. The explosions killed at least 21 people, including 15 police officers offering Friday prayers at the mosque. The attack was claimed by Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, a little-known alliance formed last April.

Article Title: Pakistan third from bottom in WEF gender gap index; women lag in workforce
Article Text:
Pakistan's women still behind in workforce

Women remain far behind men in workforce

Education drives improvement

Political representation remains low

Legal rights show gaps

NEW DELHI: Pakistan has ranked 143rd among 145 economies in the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Global Gender Gap Report 2026, placing it third from the bottom with 59.5% of its gender gap closed. Its score improved by 2.8 percentage points from 2025, marking the country's strongest year-on-year improvement in a decade, according to the report.The WEF index measures gender parity across four areas — economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment, media outlet Dawn cited.Pakistan's overall score has risen by 5.2 percentage points since 2006, when it stood at 54.3%. The WEF said the latest improvement was driven largely by gains in educational attainment.Economic participation continued to be Pakistan's weakest area, with the country scoring 36.4% and ranking 144th globally. Labour-force participation stood at 34.6% parity, while women accounted for 6.5% of legislators, senior officials and managers and 44.9% of professional and technical workers.Parity in estimated earned income stood at 26.3%. The report also found that the share of women in senior leadership and business ownership remained limited.Pakistan recorded a significant improvement in educational attainment, reaching a parity score of 91.7%, more than six percentage points higher than in the previous edition.The WEF said parity in education has improved by 21 percentage points since 2006. Gains were recorded across primary, secondary and tertiary enrolment, making education the main driver of Pakistan's overall improvement in the 2026 index.Pakistan scored 14.1% in political empowerment, ranking 107th globally. While parity in parliamentary and ministerial representation improved from the previous edition, women remained underrepresented in both areas.The report said women accounted for 21.69% of parliamentarians, while men made up 78.31%. Women held just 3.45% of ministerial positions, compared with 96.55% for men.Pakistan also received a score reflecting the period in which a woman has served as head of state, with the report noting that a female head of state had ruled the country for 4.73 of the previous 50 years.The report's contextual indicators also highlighted disparities in women's legal and economic rights. It found unequal rights relating to inheritance for widows and daughters and restricted rights in access to justice. Women were assessed as having near-equal rights regarding access to financial services and assets, while their rights relating to divorce and reproductive autonomy remained restricted.The report also recorded that 24.9% of women had experienced gender-based violence during their lives.
Article Summary: Pakistan ranked 143rd among 145 economies in the World Economic Forum’s (WEF) Global Gender Gap Report 2026. Pakistan's overall score has risen by 5.2 percentage points since 2006, when it stood at 54.3%. The WEF said the latest improvement was driven largely by gains in educational attainment.

Article Title: 'Can't afford petrol': Pakistan PTI lawmakers ride donkey carts to assembly in protest
Article Text:
(Image credit: Dawn) “The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” PTI MPA Sajjad Ali was seen saying in a video while holding a placard describing the fuel price hike as a “petrol bomb dropped on the people”.

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers and provincial lawmakers staged a protest in the Sindh province against soaring fuel prices. They arrived at the provincial assembly by riding donkey carts, saying petrol had become too expensive for them to travel in their vehicles.According to Dawn news, the protest was held after petrol prices rose to Rs 390.79 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) to Rs 424.92 per litre following the latest adjustment on Thursday. PTI MPA Sajjad Ali and other lawmakers rode donkey carts from areas near the assembly to its main gate, carrying placards and raising slogans against the federal government.“The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way on donkey carts,” Ali was seen saying in a video while holding a placard describing the fuel price hike as a “petrol bomb dropped on the people”.Ali said the protest was intended to highlight the difficulties faced by ordinary people because of rising fuel costs.“Petrol has become so expensive that we cannot even come to the assembly in our vehicles,” he said, adding that people were bearing the brunt of the government’s policies.The latest increase comes amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have disrupted major oil supply routes and pushed fuel prices higher over the past two months.The current petrol and diesel prices include government taxes and duties of Rs114 per litre on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. The government now adjusts fuel prices daily.The Pakistan bar council also criticised the repeated fuel price increases. A joint meeting of its Executive Committee and Rules Committee on Thursday called the hikes unprecedented and urged the government to take steps to control prices and provide relief to citizens.The government has meanwhile introduced a relief scheme targeting users of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqis and other two- and three-wheelers, as well as small cars with engines up to 800cc.Under the scheme, motorcycle, rickshaw and other eligible two- and three-wheeler users can receive relief on 20 litres of petrol a month. Owners of cars with engines up to 800cc are eligible for a Rs 100-per-litre relief on 30 litres of petrol each month.However, the scheme faced problems on its first day of nationwide rollout on Thursday, with several petrol pumps refusing to accept the digital app introduced for the subsidy. The pumps said they lacked the required system to sell petrol at Rs100 per litre less.The federal government also brought back austerity measures on Thursday. These include ordering markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50% for three months.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) workers and provincial lawmakers staged a protest in the Sindh province against soaring fuel prices. They arrived at the provincial assembly by riding donkey carts, saying petrol had become too expensive for them to travel in their vehicles. “The ministers and (treasury) MPAs should also reach the assembly the same way,” PTI MPA Sajjad Ali was seen saying.

Article Title: Death toll mounts to 31 in suicide blast at Pakistan police compound, several still critical
Article Text:
Army soldiers examine the site following a powerful bomb exploded at a mosque in Kohat (AP photo)

Explosives-laden car hits mosque

Militants claim responsibility

The death toll from a suicide attack on a police compound in north-western Pakistan has risen to 31, news agency AFP reported on Saturday, citing a police official.The attack took place on Friday when an explosives-packed car was driven into the police facility as officers and their families were praying at a mosque inside the compound.Around 80 people, mostly police personnel, were taken to hospital after the blast. Several injured people were in critical condition, raising fears that the death toll could increase. The number of civilian casualties was not immediately known.The attacker drove a vehicle carrying explosives into the compound shortly after noon, striking the mosque's entrance wall. The blast brought part of the building down and left the area covered in smoke and debris.Officials believe three to five gunmen, in addition to the suicide attacker who drove the vehicle, may have tried to enter the compound. Witnesses reported gunfire as the attackers attempted to force their way inside.Among those killed were an SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors from the Counter-Terrorism Department, according to sources.Videos shared on social media showed extensive damage at the site, with people fleeing the area as thick smoke rose from the compound.No group had officially claimed responsibility by late Friday. However, suspicion has fallen on Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, an umbrella alliance of three militant groups operating in the region.Another group, Inqilabi Islami Pakistan, which is affiliated with al-Qaida in the Indian subcontinent, also claimed responsibility for the attack on Telegram.Accounts supporting IMP said its Al Badr suicide unit carried out what they described as an ‘Ishtashadi operation’ at the Counter-Terrorism Department premises.Rescue teams continued clearing the site and searching for victims after the attack, while authorities assessed the full extent of the casualties.
Article Summary: Death toll from suicide attack on police compound in Kohat rises to 31. Around 80 people, mostly police personnel, were taken to hospital after the blast. Several injured people were in critical condition, raising fears that the death toll could increase. No group had officially claimed responsibility by late Friday.

Article Title: 21 security personnel dead in blast at police line in Pakistan
Article Text:
The blast was reported near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

Around 21 Pakistani security personnel were killed and dozens more injured in a suicide bombing during Friday prayers at the police lines in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Some civilians deaths are feared but their exact number could not be ascertained. The facility was struck post noon with a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device, enabling multiple attackers to force their way inside the premises, shooting indiscriminately.An SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors of the CTD were among those killed, sources said. Around 80 individuals, mostly police personnel, were admitted to hospitals for treatment. The toll is likely to rise as many of the injured were reported to be critical.No group officially claimed the attack till late Friday though the role of Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), an umbrella militant alliance formed by three armed groups operating in the region, is alleged. Another group named Inqilabi Islami Pakistan, affiliated to al-Qaida in the Indian subcontinent, also claimed the attack on Telegram.The explosion occurred near a mosque in the facility, reducing the building to rubble and prompting a major rescue and clearing operation. Three to five gunmen besides the driver of the car laden with explosives are suspected to have participated in the attack and were seen attempting to enter the police compound while exchanging fire. The car exploded after ramming into the mosque's entrance wall. Videos uploaded by locals on social media showed the extent of the damage and people frantically running for cover amid dense smoke.Pro-IMP accounts on Telegram claimed the attack, saying their Al Badr suicide brigade had carried out an 'Ishtashadi operation' at the counter-terrorism division premises.
Article Summary: The blast occurred near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. An SP-rank officer, a deputy SP and three inspectors of the CTD were among those killed, sources said. Around 80 individuals, mostly police personnel, were admitted to hospitals for treatment.

Article Title: BLA claims 43 Pakistani personnel, ‘death squad’ members killed in Balochistan
Article Text:
Balochistan sees fresh wave of violence as BLA claims 43 killed in 13 operations

The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) has claimed that 43 Pakistani military personnel and members of alleged state-backed 'death squads' were killed in 13 operations across Balochistan between September 7 and 13, according to a report.The Balochistan Post (TBP) said that in its weekly statement, BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group’s militants carried out attacks and blockades across areas including Basima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Tump, Surab, Killa Abdullah, Lasbela, Jiwani and Mashkel.The development comes as a powerful blast at a mosque inside a police compound in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killed at least 16 people and injured 57, police and rescue officials said on Friday. Five police officers and 11 civilians were among the dead. Seven armed gunmen also tried to enter the compound, with six killed in the ensuing gunfire.According to the BLA statement, the operations targeted military convoys, checkpoints and surveillance equipment, alongside people the BLA described as members of “death squads”. The group also reported attacks on commercial vehicles, bridges and a lithium extraction project.The claims could not be independently verified.The campaign allegedly began on September 7 with a five-hour blockade of a China-Pakistan Economic Corridor route in Basima, where the BLA said its fighters conducted checks. It claimed five Pakistani personnel were killed and several injured, while three BLA militants also died in the clashes.The following day, the group claimed an ambush on a military convoy in Kharan left at least four personnel killed or wounded. In Panjgur, it said militants attacked military supply vehicles and destroyed surveillance cameras.On September 10, the BLA claimed it blocked the Quetta-Taftan trade route in Chagai, seized two commercial vehicles and destroyed a bridge with explosives. It also claimed one of its units brought down a Pakistani military surveillance quadcopter in Tump.Two attacks were reported in Surab on September 11. The BLA claimed six military personnel were killed in an ambush on a convoy at Tobo, while another three were killed and four injured during a separate clash at Rodeni Cross.In Lasbela on September 12, the group claimed an attack on a military bomb-disposal convoy destroyed two vehicles and damaged two others, killing nine personnel and injuring more than 11.The BLA also claimed that 25 members of an alleged 'death squad' were killed in Killa Abdullah on September 13, followed by a four-hour clash involving Pakistani forces and the militants. Five BLA fighters were also reported killed.The group said 10 of its BLA militants were killed during the operations and vowed that its “military confrontation will continue on every front”, until Pakistani forces withdraw and an independent Balochistan is established.
Article Summary: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claims 43 Pakistani military personnel and members of alleged state-backed 'death squads' were killed in 13 operations between September 7 and 13. BLA spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said the group’s militants carried out attacks and blockades across areas including Basima, Kharan, Panjgur, Chagai, Tump, Surab and Killa Abdullah.

Article Title: Pakistan suicide blast: Mosque destroyed, people rescue survivors from under rubble - videos
Article Text:
At least 16 killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque

At least 16 people, including five police personnel, were killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque during Friday prayers at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of northwest Pakistan, as reported by the Dawn.Videos showed extensive destruction at the mosque near the old Police Lines, around 60 kilometres southwest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's capital Peshawar, following the explosion.Social media footage showed the mosque’s roof had collapsed, with rescuers and residents pulling injured people from the rubble and carrying them to ambulances.No group or individual has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.Citing District Headquarters Hospital Medical Superintendent Tahir Ali Shah, Geo News reported that 15 bodies were brought to the hospital along with more than 50 injured following the blast.Police said most of those injured were worshippers, adding that the explosion caused a crater outside the mosque.Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi said rescue teams reached the site shortly after receiving information about the blast and launched a rescue operation, as cited by PTI.He said several of the injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for initial medical treatment.Faizi said rescue teams remained at the scene and were assessing the situation.
Article Summary: At least 16 people, including five police personnel, killed and dozens injured in a suicide blast at a mosque in northwest Pakistan. The blast occurred during Friday prayers at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. No group or individual has yet claimed responsibility for the attack.

Article Title: Explosive-laden truck rams into mosque near police offices in Pakistan's Kohat; 21 dead
Article Text:
A blast was reported near the Old Police Lines in Kohat, in Pakistan’s northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

At least 21 people were killed and more than 80 injured in a suicide explosion at a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Friday, officials said.The explosion occured in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, near the Afghanistan border, during Friday prayers, bringing down part of the building and prompting a major rescue operation. Emergency responders and local residents searched through the rubble for survivors, while at least two armed gunmen attempted to storm the police compound and were killed in an exchange of fire with officers. Around three others reportedly moved towards the Special Branch building.According to Dawn, Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi said emergency teams rushed to the site after receiving information about the explosion and began rescue operations.The injured were taken to nearby hospitals for treatment, while roads leading to the blast site were closed, Geo News reported. Rescue teams remained at the scene to assess the situation.The location was initially described by rescue officials as being near the Old Police Lines.However, a statement from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa inspector general Zulfiqar Hameed said the explosion occurred at a mosque inside the Police Lines complex.“Following the explosion, an exchange of fire ensued with the armed terrorists,” the statement said. Hameed also directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for those injured in the blast.Separately, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister Sohail Afridi and governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the explosion and expressed solidarity with those affected. The blast comes a day after a roadside bomb targeted a security forces convoy in northwestern Hangu district, killing six soldiers. Additionally government forces carried out raids in several areas on Thursday and killed 10 militants suspected to be affiliated with the Pakistani Taliban.Footage circulating on social media showed the roof of the mosque had collapsed. Rescuers and local residents could be seen pulling injured people from the rubble and carrying them to ambulances.The attack was claimed by a seperatist group led by Hafiz Gul Bahadur. Suspicion could nevertheless fall on the Pakistani Taliban, or Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which has carried out repeated attacks against security personnel and civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, AP said.In 2023, a suicide bombing at a mosque in Peshawar, the provincial capital, killed 101 people. The TTP is separate from Afghanistan's Taliban but maintains an alliance with the group.Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Taliban government in Kabul of providing shelter to TTP members and allowing cross-border attacks to be carried out from Afghan territory. Kabul has denied the allegations.Authorities have yet to establish the precise nature of Friday's explosion or identify those responsible. Further details are expected as investigators assess the scene and the condition of those injured.
Article Summary: At least 21 people were killed and more than 80 injured in a suicide explosion at a mosque inside the Kohat Police Lines in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The explosion occured during Friday prayers, bringing down part of the building and prompting a major rescue operation. At least two armed gunmen attempted to storm the police compound and were killed in an exchange of fire with officers.

Article Title: No official dinners, foreign travel: Pakistan rolls out austerity measures amid fuel shock
Article Text:
Fuel shock hits Pakistan

Pakistan on Thursday announced a fresh set of austerity measures, including a 50 per cent cut in fuel allocations for government vehicles and a ban on official foreign travel and the purchase of new government vehicles. The measures come as rising global oil prices threaten fuel, gas and power supplies.The measures, approved by the Pakistan cabinet, will remain in force for three months as the government seeks to reduce fuel consumption and public expenditure.Under the new restrictions, markets will have to close by 9 pm, while marriage halls can operate until 10 pm and restaurants until 11 pm. Drug stores and medical laboratories have been exempted.Fuel allocations for government vehicles will be reduced by half, although vehicles used by the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and essential services will not be covered by the cut.The Shehbaz Sharif government has also ordered a five per cent reduction in non-employee-related expenditure and prohibited official foreign visits and domestic travel for meetings, directing officials to use virtual meetings instead.Official dinners have been banned, except those hosted for foreign visitors and delegations. The purchase of new government vehicles has also been prohibited, while procurement of durable goods has been restricted, with IT purchases exempted.The measures come two days after Pakistan raised petrol prices by PkR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by PkR 6.41 per litre. Petrol now costs PkR 384.34 per litre, while HSD is priced at PkR 415.83.Global oil prices have risen amid continuing conflict and supply concerns in West Asia, including attacks on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and the temporary closure of its East-West oil pipeline following an aerial attack.The austerity package is the second such effort this year. Pakistan introduced similar measures in March, including a temporary school shutdown, reductions in government fuel use and greater reliance on remote working.Earlier the government had introduced the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme from Wednesday, offering motorcycle, rickshaw and small-car owners a subsidy of 100 rupees (36 US cents) per litre on a capped monthly quota.The programme, however, has faced implementation difficulties. Karachi resident Mohammad Musharraf told Reuters: "First of all, you have to register your vehicle. Then you have to register your mobile phone. How can an illiterate person survive if the conditions are so difficult?"The energy pressures extend beyond transport. Reuters reported that Pakistan's power sector could require up to 400 million cubic feet of gas a day through winter, while only two LNG cargoes had been confirmed for September.
Article Summary: Pakistan announces new austerity measures, including a 50 per cent cut in fuel allocations for government vehicles and a ban on official foreign travel. The measures come as rising global oil prices threaten fuel, gas and power supplies. Pakistan raised petrol prices by PkR 4.10 per litre and high-speed diesel by PKR 6.41 per litres.

Article Title: Indian-origin climber Dhrubajyoti Guha, Nepalese guide killed in Manaslu avalanche
Article Text:
Dhrubajyoti Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur (now IIEST Shibpur), in 2002.

TOI

An Indian-origin climber and his Nepalese Sherpa guide were killed in an overnight avalanche at Camp 3 on Mount Manaslu (8,163m) after they continued towards the summit while six other climbers turned back amid worsening weather, expedition organisers said on Sunday. Rescuers found Dhrubajyoti Guha and Fursemba Sherpa, both 47, buried inside their tent, taking the autumn season toll on the world’s eighth-highest peak to four.Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur (now IIEST Shibpur), in 2002. He had worked with ABB, IBM, Pfizer and Nestlé and was an accomplished ultra-endurance trail runner with 32 UTMB World Series race finishes, including several over 100km. Sherpa was an NMA-registered guide from Nepal’s Makalu region who had summited Everest nine times and also climbed Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, Cho Oyu and Manaslu.Mohan Lamsal, managing director of expedition organiser Makalu Adventure, said conditions deteriorated as the group reached the higher camps. “Six other climbers who decided to retreat from Camp 2 are safe, but Guha and Sherpa decided to make an early summit attempt and headed for Camp III on Saturday evening,” Lamsal toldContact with the two was lost overnight. “We were alerted around 11.30am on Sunday after they stopped responding. We immediately sent four Sherpa climbers to Camp III to look for them. They dug through the snow and found both inside their tent, buried beneath nearly seven feet of snow,” Lamsal said.Continuing snowfall and avalanche risk prevented the rescuers from bringing the bodies to base camp. “I asked the rescue team to descend to the lower camps because it was not safe to remain there. We will try to bring the bodies down once the weather improves,” Lamsal said.Heavy snowfall began on Friday evening and continued through Sunday, with up to 60cm recorded at base camp, forcing hundreds of climbers to retreat or remain at lower camps. Some teams had begun ascending on Saturday in anticipation of a relatively favourable weather window from Monday, but meteorologists had warned of another spell of bad weather around Wednesday as a system developing over the Bay of Bengal was expected to affect the region.The deaths followed two earlier fatalities on Manaslu this autumn. Singaporean climber Lau Wee Seng, 50, died at around 6,000m while descending from Camp 2 on Sept 17, while Tashi Sherpa, 20, a Nepali high-altitude worker, was found dead inside a tent at base camp on Sept 5.Manaslu has drawn a record 480 foreign climbers this autumn, accompanied by more than 500 Nepali guides and support staff. The latest fatalities took the number of reported mountaineering deaths across the Himalayas and Karakoram this year to at least 24, making 2026 one of the deadliest for climbers in the region in recent years.
Article Summary: Dhrubajyoti Guha and Fursemba Sherpa, both 47, buried inside their tent. The autumn season toll on the world’s eighth-highest peak to four. Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur.

Article Title: ‘Treated on floor, verandah’: Dhaka hospitals struggle to find space for dengue patients
Article Text:
Patients infected with dengue receive treatment at a hospital in Dhaka

Patients treated on floors, verandas

Dengue spreads beyond Dhaka

October could bring further rise

A sharp rise in dengue cases is putting hospitals in Dhaka under severe pressure. Over 747 new patients were admitted across Bangladesh in the 24 hours to 8am on Friday. The surge prompted some hospitals to treat patients on floors and verandas after beds filled up.According to a report by Dhaka Tribune, at Mugda General Hospital in Dhaka, 145 dengue patients were receiving treatment in a ward with a capacity of just 38 beds on Thursday. Doctors and nurses said the overcrowding was making it harder to monitor patients, administer medicines and provide emergency care.The directorate general of health services (DGHS) said no dengue deaths were reported during the latest 24-hour period. However, 79 dengue deaths have been recorded in the first 18 days of September alone.Since January 1, 59,147 people have been hospitalised with dengue across Bangladesh, with 176 deaths reported. A total of 54,838 patients have been discharged after treatment.At Mugda General Hospital, every designated bed in the dengue ward was occupied. Additional patients were being treated on the floor and veranda, while some beds were being shared by more than one patient.Afrin Akter, from Narayanganj, was among those being treated on the floor. She was vomiting intermittently and appeared too weak to speak properly as a nurse administered saline.Her mother said Afrin had suffered from fever and body aches for several days. After medicines failed to improve her condition, the family tried to get her admitted to several hospitals but could not find a vacant bed.They eventually reached Mugda General Hospital, where Afrin was admitted despite the lack of a bed.Nasima, sub-in-charge of the hospital, said patients were arriving every day from Dhaka and districts outside the capital.“Due to the bed shortage, patients are being admitted to the floor and veranda out of necessity,” she said.She said 145 patients were currently being treated in the ward against its capacity of 38 beds. Many patients, she added, arrive in critical condition, while early treatment can improve the chances of recovery.Dr Nurul Islam, deputy director of Mugda General Hospital, said the increase in dengue cases had pushed up patient pressure.“At present, services are being continued with the existing doctors and nurses, but additional beds and manpower are needed to handle the situation,” he said.“All the patients who are coming here are being admitted and provided treatment. Instructions have been given to every ward to provide proper treatment.”The latest DGHS figures show that the pressure is not limited to the capital.Of the 747 patients admitted nationwide in the latest 24-hour period, 216 were admitted outside Dhaka's city corporations but within Dhaka division. Another 61 were admitted in Dhaka North City and 40 in Dhaka South.Chittagong division recorded 180 admissions, while 92 patients were admitted in Mymensingh, 81 in Khulna, 52 in Rangpur and 25 in Barisal.August was the worst month for dengue this year, with 20,536 infections and 43 deaths reported.Entomologist professor Kabirul Bashar said forecast models indicate that the dengue situation could worsen further in October.Although Aedes mosquitoes become less visible as winter approaches, he said they should not be neglected.Referring to Bangladesh as a “country of mosquitoes,” Bashar said dengue cases were rising compared with previous years and warned that the situation could become more severe in the coming days.He called for greater public awareness about Aedes mosquito behaviour and stronger mosquito-control measures.DGHS director general professor Dr Prabhat Chandra Biswas said patients would be referred to private hospitals if government facilities exceeded their capacity.He said hospitals had been instructed to increase their bed capacity and that treatment facilities were also being strengthened at district and upazila levels in dengue-prone areas.Public health expert Dr Mushtak Hossain said treating patients alone would not be enough to control the outbreak.“The long-term effective solution is to destroy the breeding grounds of Aedes mosquitoes,” he said.He called for regular mosquito control, greater public awareness and early detection and treatment at the local level, along with adequate facilities in Dhaka and across districts and upazilas.
Article Summary: Over 747 new patients were admitted across Bangladesh in the 24 hours to 8am on Friday. At Mugda General Hospital in Dhaka, 145 dengue patients were receiving treatment in a ward with a capacity of 38 beds. Doctors and nurses said the overcrowding was making it harder to monitor patients, administer medicines and provide emergency care.

Article Title: From July Uprising leader to graft probe: Former Yunus govt advisor Asif Mahmud under scanner
Article Text:
Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain (Courtesy: Facebook)

Bangladesh’s anti-graft agency said Friday it has sought details of the financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, a prominent leader of the 2024 “July Uprising” that ousted the Sheikh Hasina government, as part of a money-laundering investigation.Mahmud and his wife have been accused of laundering $1.05 billion during his tenure as an adviser in the Muhammad Yunus-led interim administration, which governed Bangladesh following Sheikh Hasina’s ouster. The Yunus-led administration stepped down after the February 12 elections, which were won by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).“We have asked the Financial Intelligence Unit to provide comprehensive information on the financial transactions and assets of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and his wife,” an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) spokesman told reporters, PTI reported.A key allegation against Bhuyain is that he was involved in laundering Taka 11,000 crore across five countries, including Taka 4,500 crore allegedly siphoned off to Dubai. He is also accused of using illicit funds to purchase land in Portugal.Bhuyain has said that, if found guilty, he would rather serve a prison sentence than flee the country.The ACC has reportedly received more than 2,000 written complaints against advisors and officials of the interim administration.ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan previously denied allegations that Bhuyain was being deliberately targeted, saying the proceedings against him were being conducted strictly in accordance with the law.The anti-graft body launched its investigation on September 2 and has since obtained documents from the local government and youth ministries, which Bhuyain headed during the interim administration.Before leaving office, advisors to the interim government disclosed their wealth statements. Bhuyain, who reportedly did not have a Taxpayer Identification Number before joining the administration, declared assets worth Taka 15.3 lakh at the time.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's anti-graft agency seeks details of financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain. He is a prominent leader of the 2024 “July Uprising” that ousted the Sheikh Hasina government. He and his wife have been accused of laundering $1.05 billion during his tenure as an adviser.
